idiom_name: cpp-httplib Server::Get handler lambda per page (Crow/Drogon equivalent)
implementation_notes: A header-only HTTP library supplies the dispatch but not the pattern: svr.Get("/orders", handler) maps one path to one lambda, so the lambda is the page controller, httplib::Request carries the parsed request and httplib::Response::set_content selects the outcome. Nothing corresponds to a container's controller base class, so shared behaviour is either registered once on the server (pre/post-routing hooks, error handler, logger) or factored into a hand-written helper called by each page - the first is already the front-controller direction. Prefer the thin handler-per-page form for page-scoped sites; move to Crow or Drogon only when their middleware and templating are actually needed, since the full page-controller structure remains hand-written in all of them.
pitfalls: Handlers run on the server's worker threads: repositories or caches captured by reference must be thread-safe, and a blocking handler holds its thread (the library is explicitly blocking I/O).
Lambdas capture by reference: any object they point at must outlive svr.listen(), or the page crashes only under production traffic.
Without a framework there is no view layer: templating, escaping and error pages are your responsibility, and forgetting to escape model data is a direct XSS path.
